title: नवमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 9 · The women of Hastinapura lament

summary.en: Janamejaya asks what Dhritarashtra did after Vyasa left, and the city rings with the cries of the women. The Kuru women come out in a single garment, with hair loose, to go to the field where their husbands lie.
summary.kn: ವ್ಯಾಸರು ಹೋದ ಮೇಲೆ ಧೃತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರ ಏನು ಮಾಡಿದನೆಂದು ಜನಮೇಜಯ ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ; ನಗರ ಸ್ತ್ರೀಯರ ಆಕ್ರಂದನದಿಂದ ಮೊಳಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂಟಿ ವಸ್ತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೂದಲು ಬಿಚ್ಚಿ ಕುರು ಸ್ತ್ರೀಯರು ಗಂಡಂದಿರು ಮಲಗಿರುವ ರಣರಂಗಕ್ಕೆ ಹೊರಡುತ್ತಾರೆ.
summary.hi: जनमेजय पूछते हैं कि व्यास के जाने पर धृतराष्ट्र ने क्या किया, और नगर स्त्रियों के विलाप से गूँज उठता है। कुरु स्त्रियाँ एक वस्त्र में, केश खोले, उस रणभूमि को जाती हैं जहाँ उनके पति पड़े हैं।
summary.te: వ్యాసుడు వెళ్లాక ధృతరాష్ట్రుడు ఏం చేశాడని జనమేజయుడు అడుగుతాడు; నగరం స్త్రీల ఆక్రందనలతో మార్మోగుతుంది. కురు స్త్రీలు ఒకే వస్త్రంతో, జుట్టు విరబోసుకుని భర్తలు పడి ఉన్న రణభూమికి బయలుదేరతారు.
summary.ta: வியாசர் சென்றபின் த்ருதராஷ்டிரன் என்ன செய்தான் என்று ஜனமேஜயன் கேட்க, நகரம் பெண்களின் அழுகையால் எதிரொலிக்கிறது. குருப் பெண்கள் ஒற்றை ஆடையுடன் கூந்தல் விரித்துக் கணவர் கிடக்கும் களத்துக்குச் செல்கின்றனர்.
summary.ml: വ്യാസൻ പോയ ശേഷം ധൃതരാഷ്ട്രർ എന്തു ചെയ്തുവെന്ന് ജനമേജയൻ ചോദിക്കുന്നു; നഗരം സ്ത്രീകളുടെ നിലവിളികളാൽ മുഴങ്ങുന്നു. ഭർത്താക്കന്മാർ കിടക്കുന്ന യുദ്ധക്കളത്തിലേക്ക് പോകാൻ കുരുവംശത്തിലെ സ്ത്രീകൾ ഒറ്റവസ്ത്രത്തിൽ, മുടി അഴിച്ചിട്ട് പുറത്തിറങ്ങുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 11.9; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Apr 17 2017

verses.text: जनमेजय उवाच

meaning.en: Janamejaya said:

verses.text:
गते भगवति व्यासे धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः ।
किमचेष्टत विप्रर्षे तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥

meaning.en: When the blessed Vyasa had gone, brahmin sage, what did King Dhritarashtra do? You should tell me this.

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा नरश्रेष्ठ चिरं ध्यात्वा त्वचेतनः ।
संजयं योजयेत्युक्त्वा विदुरं प्रत्यभाषत ॥

meaning.en: Hearing this, best of men, he brooded long, dazed, and then said to Vidura, "Make Sanjaya ready."

verses.text:
क्षिप्रमानय गान्धारीं सर्वाश्च भरतस्त्रियः ।
वधूं कुन्तीमुपादाय याश्चान्यास्तत्र योषितः ॥

meaning.en: He said: "Bring Gandhari quickly, and all the women of the Bharata house, with my daughter-in-law Kunti and any other women there."

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा स धर्मात्मा विदुरं धर्मवित्तमम् ।
शोकविप्रहतज्ञानो यानमेवान्वपद्यत ॥

meaning.en: Having said this to Vidura, the best knower of dharma, the righteous king, his mind shattered by grief, got into a carriage.

verses.text:
गान्धारी चैव शोकार्ता भर्तुर्वचनचोदिता ।
सह कुन्त्या यतो राजा सह स्त्रीभिरुपाद्रवत् ॥

meaning.en: Gandhari too, afflicted with grief and urged on by her husband's words, hurried with Kunti and the women to where the king was.

verses.text:
ताः समासाद्य राजानं भृशं शोकसमन्विताः ।
आमन्त्र्यान्योन्यमीयुः स्म भृशमुच्चुक्रुशुस्ततः ॥

meaning.en: Reaching the king, they were full of sorrow, greeted one another, and then cried out loudly.

verses.text:
ताः समाश्वासयत्क्षत्ता ताभ्यश्चार्ततरः स्वयम् ।
अश्रुकण्ठीः समारोप्य ततोऽसौ निर्ययौ पुरात् ॥

meaning.en: Vidura comforted them, though he himself was more distressed than they. With tears choking their throats, he placed them in carriages and left the city.

verses.text:
ततः प्रणादः संजज्ञे सर्वेषु कुरुवेश्मसु ।
आकुमारं पुरं सर्वमभवच्छोककर्शितम् ॥

meaning.en: Then a wail rose from all the Kuru houses, and the whole city, down to the children, was wasted with grief.

verses.text:
अदृष्टपूर्वा या नार्यः पुरा देवगणैरपि ।
पृथग्जनेन दृश्यन्त तास्तदा निहतेश्वराः ॥

meaning.en: Women who had never before been seen even by the hosts of gods were then seen by common people, their lords slain.

verses.text:
प्रकीर्य केशान्सुशुभान्भूषणान्यवमुच्य च ।
एकवस्त्रधरा नार्यः परिपेतुरनाथवत् ॥

meaning.en: With their lovely hair loosened and their ornaments cast off, wearing a single garment, the women rushed out like those with no protector.

verses.text:
श्वेतपर्वतरूपेभ्यो गृहेभ्यस्तास्त्वपाक्रमन् ।
गुहाभ्य इव शैलानां पृषत्यो हतयूथपाः ॥

meaning.en: They came out of houses that looked like white mountains, like doe with their herd-leaders killed coming from mountain caves.

verses.text:
तान्युदीर्णानि नारीणां तदा वृन्दान्यनेकशः ।
शोकार्तान्यद्रवन्राजन्किशोरीणामिवाङ्गने ॥

meaning.en: Rising in many groups, those women, afflicted with grief, ran like young girls in a courtyard, king.

verses.text:
प्रगृह्य बाहून्क्रोशन्त्यः पुत्रान्भ्रातॄन्पितॄनपि ।
दर्शयन्तीव ता ह स्म युगान्ते लोकसंक्षयम् ॥

meaning.en: Raising their arms and crying out for their sons, brothers and fathers, they seemed to show the destruction of the world at the end of an age.

verses.text:
विलपन्त्यो रुदन्त्यश्च धावमानास्ततस्ततः ।
शोकेनाभ्याहतज्ञानाः कर्तव्यं न प्रजज्ञिरे ॥

meaning.en: Wailing, weeping and running here and there, their reason struck by grief, they did not know what they should do.

verses.text:
व्रीडां जग्मुः पुरा याः स्म सखीनामपि योषितः ।
ता एकवस्त्रा निर्लज्जाः श्वश्रूणां पुरतोऽभवन् ॥

meaning.en: Women who had once been shy even before their friends stood now in a single garment, shameless, before their mothers-in-law.

verses.text:
परस्परं सुसूक्ष्मेषु शोकेष्वाश्वासयन्स्म याः ।
ताः शोकविह्वला राजन्नुपैक्षन्त परस्परम् ॥

meaning.en: Those who had once comforted one another in the slightest griefs now, overwhelmed with sorrow, looked on one another without notice, king.

verses.text:
ताभिः परिवृतो राजा रुदतीभिः सहस्रशः ।
निर्ययौ नगराद्दीनस्तूर्णमायोधनं प्रति ॥

meaning.en: The king, surrounded by thousands of weeping women, left the city, wretched, and hurried to the battlefield.

verses.text:
शिल्पिनो वणिजो वैश्याः सर्वकर्मोपजीविनः ।
ते पार्थिवं पुरस्कृत्य निर्ययुर्नगराद्बहिः ॥

meaning.en: Craftsmen, merchants, vaishyas and all who lived by various works came out of the city behind the king.

verses.text:
तासां विक्रोशमानानामार्तानां कुरुसंक्षये ।
प्रादुरासीन्महाञ्शब्दो व्यथयन्भुवनान्युत ॥

meaning.en: As the afflicted women cried out over the destruction of the Kurus, a great noise arose that pained the worlds.

verses.text:
युगान्तकाले संप्राप्ते भूतानां दह्यतामिव ।
अभावः स्यादयं प्राप्त इति भूतानि मेनिरे ॥

meaning.en: As at the coming of the end of an age, when beings seem to burn, creatures thought that annihilation had arrived.

verses.text:
भृशमुद्विग्नमनसस्ते पौराः कुरुसंक्षये ।
प्राक्रोशन्त महाराज स्वनुरक्तास्तदा भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: The townspeople, deeply distressed at the destruction of the Kurus, loved them dearly and cried out loudly, great king.
